title: Just Five More Minutes

pre.en: Why does Chen pick up his phone at the end of the story?
pre.zh: 故事最后，小陈为什么又拿起了手机？
options: To find out how to stop the clock ticking

intro: 一个新概念式的小故事：小陈每晚都发誓十一点前上床，可一拿起手机就停不下来。妹妹要来伦敦了，他决定换个办法。读的时候留意频率的说法：usually、hardly ever 这类副词放在 be 动词后、实义动词前；every other day、once in a while 这类短语多放在句尾。结尾有个小反转。

sentences.en: Every night, Chen tells himself the same thing: tonight he'll be in bed by eleven.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上，小陈都跟自己说同一句话：今晚十一点前一定上床。

sentences.en: To be fair, his evenings are usually fine.
sentences.zh: 其实他晚上一般都挺正常的。

sentences.en: He's home by half past six and cooks at seven.
sentences.zh: 六点半到家，七点做饭。

sentences.en: He watches something with Tom every other day, and once in a while he goes for a walk.
sentences.zh: 隔一天跟 Tom 一起看点什么，偶尔还出去散散步。

sentences.en: He hardly ever drinks coffee after lunch.
sentences.zh: 午饭以后，他几乎从来不喝咖啡。

sentences.en: The problem starts at a quarter to eleven.
sentences.zh: 问题出在十点四十五。

sentences.en: He picks up his phone, just to check the weather.
sentences.zh: 他拿起手机，说是只看一眼天气。

sentences.en: Then he comes across a video of a man cleaning old trainers, then another.
sentences.zh: 结果刷到一个男的洗旧球鞋的视频，接着又是一个。

sentences.en: Honestly, he can't put the phone down until one.
sentences.zh: 说真的，不到一点，他根本放不下手机。

sentences.en: And every night, he says it's the last time he'll stay up late.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上他都说，这是最后一次熬夜。

sentences.en: His sister Lily is a nurse, and she's got strong opinions about sleep.
sentences.zh: 他妹妹 Lily 是护士，在睡觉这件事上特别较真。

sentences.en: She's coming to stay for three months, and she lands at Heathrow on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 她要来他这儿住三个月，周六在希思罗机场落地。

sentences.en: When he told her about his evenings, she wasn't impressed.
sentences.zh: 他跟她说了自己晚上的情况，她听了直摇头。

sentences.en: "It's a good idea to stop using screens an hour before bed," she said.
sentences.zh: 「睡前一个小时最好别再看屏幕，」她说。

sentences.en: "Your brain needs time to wind down."
sentences.zh: 「你的大脑得有时间慢慢静下来。」

sentences.en: So on Thursday, he tries a new plan.
sentences.zh: 于是周四，他换了个新办法。

sentences.en: He leaves his phone in the kitchen and buys a £6 alarm clock from the corner shop.
sentences.zh: 他把手机留在厨房，又在街角小店买了个 6 英镑的闹钟。

sentences.en: The owner insists on showing him the ropes, even though it's only got two buttons.
sentences.zh: 店老板非要手把手教他怎么用，虽然那闹钟一共就两个按钮。

sentences.en: "This one sets the alarm, and this one turns it off."
sentences.zh: 「这个定闹钟，这个关掉。」

sentences.en: Six pounds for a clock that must be thirty years old is a bit of a rip-off.
sentences.zh: 一个少说也有三十年的旧钟卖 6 英镑，有点坑。

sentences.en: By half past ten, he's switched off the light and feels he's making progress.
sentences.zh: 十点半，他已经关了灯，觉得自己总算有进步了。

sentences.en: Then he hears it: tick, tick, tick.
sentences.zh: 然后他听见了：嘀嗒，嘀嗒，嘀嗒。

sentences.en: The clock is so loud that at twenty to one, he's still wide awake.
sentences.zh: 钟走得太响了，到了十二点四十，他还是一点睡意都没有。

sentences.en: He lies there, keeping an eye on the red hand.
sentences.zh: 他就那么躺着，盯着那根红色的秒针。

sentences.en: He goes through his options: a pillow, a drawer, the window.
sentences.zh: 他把办法挨个想了一遍：拿枕头捂上、塞进抽屉、扔出窗外。

sentences.en: In the end, he gets up, goes into the kitchen and picks up his phone — to search "how to stop a clock ticking".
sentences.zh: 最后，他爬起来走进厨房，拿起手机——搜「怎么让钟不嘀嗒响」。

cards.note: to lift something, or to collect something that is waiting for you
to find something or meet someone when you are not looking for them
cards.tip: 强调「没在找」；come 的过去式是 came。
cards.example: I came across an old photo of my parents in a book.

cards.note: 英式说法，常用复数；美式说 sneakers。
to find something so interesting that you cannot stop reading, watching or using it
cards.tip: 常说书好看：I couldn't put it down。代词要放中间：put it down，不说 put down it。
cards.example: The book was so good that I couldn't put it down.

cards.note: to go to bed much later than usual
cards.tip: stay up 是「不去睡」，late 可以换成具体时间：stay up until two。别和 get up late（起得晚）混。
cards.example: We stayed up late talking about the trip.

cards.note: not impressed 常是委婉的「不满意、不以为然」。
used to give advice in a friendly way
to relax after a busy or exciting time, especially before sleep
cards.tip: 这里的 wind 读 /waɪnd/，过去式 wound 读 /waʊnd/；和「风」wind /wɪnd/ 不是一个词。
cards.example: I usually read for half an hour to wind down after work.

cards.note: 英国街区里卖牛奶、面包、零食的小店，营业时间长。
后面接 on doing：insist on paying（非要付钱）。

cards.zh: 教某人入门；带某人熟悉门道
cards.note: to teach someone how to do a job or how things work in a new place
to make a clock or phone ring at a certain time
cards.tip: 定在几点用 for：set an alarm for six；闹钟响了说 the alarm goes off。set 的过去式、过去分词都是 set。
cards.example: Can you set an alarm for half past five?

cards.note: something that costs much more than it should
cards.tip: 口语词，名词；动词是 rip sb off（宰某人）：They ripped us off。
cards.example: Eight pounds for a sandwich? That's a rip-off.

cards.note: to turn off a light or machine; also, to stop thinking about work and relax
cards.tip: 英式更常说 switch off，美式多说 turn off；人当主语时是「放空、不想事」。
cards.example: I can't switch off when I'm on holiday — I keep checking emails.

cards.note: to improve, or to move forward towards a goal
也指打勾：tick the box（在方框里打勾）。

cards.zh: 完全清醒；一点睡意都没有
cards.note: to be completely awake, often when you want to be asleep
cards.tip: wide 在这里是「完全」，只和 awake、open 这几个词连用：wide open。反义是 fast asleep（第 1 课）。
cards.example: It was three in the morning and the baby was wide awake.

cards.note: to watch something or someone carefully so that nothing bad happens
cards.tip: 也可以是「帮忙照看」：keep an eye on my bag。keep 的过去式是 kept。
cards.example: Could you keep an eye on the soup while I answer the door?

cards.note: 时针 hour hand，分针 minute hand，秒针 second hand。
to look at or check something carefully from beginning to end
枕套是 pillowcase。
读 /drɔː/，w 和 er 基本不发音。
after a long time, or after a lot of problems
